args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks across all production regions following the v2.3.1 deploy. Observed state: all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) on v2.3.1, healthy=false, error rate ~18%. Action taken: rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production (v2.2.9 was also healthy but older; v2.3.1-rc is a staging build and was unhealthy). The first rollback attempt partially failed — the rollout halted after us-east due to an orchestrator error, leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout. Current state: all three regions on v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate ~0.2%. No approval was required since v2.3.0 has previously been healthy in production. Follow-up: root-cause the v2.3.1 health check failures before any redeploy, and verify error rate remains at baseline.

trace.final:
Done — exactly one incident exists, so the retry did not duplicate it.

## Summary

**Target release:** v2.3.0 — the most recent release healthy in production. Release history showed v2.2.9 (healthy, older), v2.3.0 (healthy), v2.3.1 (unhealthy, seq 3), and v2.3.1-rc (staging build, unhealthy — excluded).

**Rollback:** The first attempt failed partway with a partial failure (`Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error`), leaving production in a mixed state: us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on the broken v2.3.1. I re-checked status to confirm that, then retried, which completed the rollout to all three regions.

**Verified recovery:** `v2.3.0` in us-east, us-west, eu-west; `healthy: true`; error rate down from **18% → 0.2%**.

**Incident:** INC-0001, SEV2, open, on-call paged. The summary records the v2.3.1 failure, the rollback, the partial-failure-and-retry, and follow-up to root-cause v2.3.1 before redeploying.

**Approval:** None needed. The change-manager approval requirement applies only to deploying a version never healthy in production; v2.3.0 had prior healthy production status, and this was a rollback rather than a new deploy.

Two things worth flagging for follow-up: the orchestrator error that truncated the first rollback attempt may indicate a control-plane issue worth investigating separately, and v2.3.1 remains the latest built version, so it should not be redeployed until the health check failures are understood.
